belief: I have to be useful to be wanted.
origins: Some of us learned that we were welcome when we helped: when we cooked, listened, fixed, drove, or gave. If affection came mostly when we were useful, we learned that our value was our usefulness. As adults, we may say yes to everything, feel panic at being a guest, and quietly wonder whether anyone would want us around without what we provide.
teaches: Paul writes, “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” John says, “Love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.” The LORD “will rejoice over you with gladness; He will quiet you with His love.” Accepted by Christ, we are told, “Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you.” God wants you, not just what you do. Serving others is a good thing, but it is not the price of belonging.
self_statements: If I stop helping, they will drop me.
I am only wanted when I am needed.
I cannot just be a guest.
My value is in what I give.
If I say no, I will be left out.
errors: Predicting rejection if I stop being useful.
Believing I am either useful and wanted or useless and unwanted.
Insisting that I must always contribute.
Feeling anxious when not helping and concluding I am unwanted.
questions: When did I learn that I am wanted for what I do?
Has anyone enjoyed my company when I was not doing anything useful?
What would happen if I said no to one request?
What would it be like to receive without giving back?
Who could I simply enjoy time with?
truth: I am wanted for who I am, not only for what I provide. God’s love was given before I did anything, and I can be with others without earning my place. I can serve out of love, not out of fear of being dropped.
hw_truths: I am wanted for who I am.
Service is a gift, not a fee.
I can receive as well as give.
Rest does not cost me love.
I can enjoy people without being useful.
log: Each week, spend time with someone without doing anything for them and note how it felt.
actions: Write when you say yes out of fear.
Decline a small request kindly and see what happens.
Accept help or a compliment without repaying it.
Let it settle that God delights in you.
prayer: Lord, I have tried to earn my place. Thank You that You love me first. Teach me to rest in being wanted and to serve out of love, not fear. Amen.
hw_questions: When did I learn I am wanted for usefulness?
What would a no cost me?
Who can I just be with?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God loved me first, so I do not have to earn my place.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I have to be useful to be wanted.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
